issues.legal_issue: An easement by implied grant may be recognized where the circumstances of a property’s separate allotment and the established use of a pathway show that the pathway was intended for access to the allotted property.
material_facts: The properties were originally held together, and one property was later allotted for separate residential use while the pathway remained within property controlled by others.
The pathway had been used continuously to reach the residential property from at least the time the building was occupied.
No other pathway for access was established by the opposing parties.
The pathway’s use was not objected to for many years, and the evidence supported an intention that it serve access to the separately allotted property.
issues.conclusion: The circumstances supported an implied grant of an easement over the pathway, and the declaration of that easement was upheld.
issues.legal_principle: An easement may arise by implied grant when the intention to grant can be inferred from the terms of the grant or the surrounding circumstances. The Court relied on the discussion of implied and constructive grants in Katiyar’s Law of Easements and Licences and on Annapurna Dutta v. Santosh Kumar Sett & Ors., AIR 1937 Cal. 661, which explains that an ordinary right of way does not ordinarily pass on severance absent language creating it, subject to circumstances such as a formed road or permanence in the adaptation of the property. The Court distinguished an easement of grant from an easement of necessity, which ends when necessity ends.

rule.if: easement_declaration_case and property_separated_for_distinct_use and pathway_used_continuously_for_access and no_alternative_access_established and pathway_use_not_objected_to

predicates.easement_declaration_case: The proceeding seeks recognition of an easement over a pathway for access to property.
predicates.property_separated_for_distinct_use: A property was allotted for separate use while the pathway remained within property controlled by another.
predicates.pathway_used_continuously_for_access: The claimant or occupier repeatedly used the pathway to reach the separately used property.
predicates.no_alternative_access_established: The opposing party did not establish another pathway providing access to the property.
predicates.pathway_use_not_objected_to: The pathway was used for access without objection for a substantial period.

issues.definition: When a property is separated for distinct use, a pathway is continuously used to access it, no alternative access is established, and that use is not objected to, an easement over the pathway may be recognized as impliedly granted.

issues.legal_issue: A decree based on an implied grant of an easement may be supported even when implied grant was not specifically pleaded, if the parties understood and contested that issue and adduced evidence on it.
material_facts: The claimant pleaded an easement by grant, although the pleading did not specifically characterize the grant as implied.
Both sides understood and contested whether an implied grant existed and adduced evidence on that issue.
The trial court considered the pleadings and evidence and found an easement by grant.
issues.conclusion: The absence of a specific pleading of implied grant did not prevent the courts from granting relief on that basis.
issues.legal_principle: A specific pleading of implied grant is not necessary when the parties understood the issue and adduced evidence to prove and contest it. The Court held that the concurrent factual findings did not warrant interference under Article 136 of the Constitution of India.

rule.if: civil_easement_suit and implied_grant_not_specifically_pleaded and parties_understood_and_contested_implied_grant and evidence_adduced_on_implied_grant

predicates.civil_easement_suit: The proceeding seeks relief for an asserted easement.
predicates.implied_grant_not_specifically_pleaded: The pleading does not expressly identify implied grant as the basis of the easement claim.
predicates.parties_understood_and_contested_implied: Both sides understood that the existence of an implied grant was at issue and presented opposing positions on it.
predicates.evidence_adduced_on_implied_grant: The parties presented evidence relevant to whether an implied grant existed.

issues.definition: If an easement claim does not specifically plead implied grant but both parties understand and contest that basis and present evidence on it, implied grant may support the decree.

issues.legal_issue: The Supreme Court does not interfere under Article 136 with concurrent factual findings supported by the evidence when the parties understood and litigated the factual issue.
material_facts: The trial court and first appellate court concurrently found that the pathway had been used for access to the residential property.
The parties had understood and presented evidence on the implied-grant issue.
The High Court affirmed the concurrent findings, and the Supreme Court found no basis to disturb them.
issues.conclusion: The concurrent factual findings were left undisturbed, and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: The Court declined to upset the concurrent findings of fact in the exercise of its powers under Article 136 of the Constitution of India, particularly where the parties had understood and adduced evidence on the issue.

rule.if: special_leave_appeal_from_concurrent_findings and findings_are_factual and findings_are_supported_by_evidence and issue_was_understood_and_litigated

predicates.special_leave_appeal_from_concurrent_fin: The proceeding is a special-leave appeal challenging factual findings affirmed by successive courts.
predicates.findings_are_factual: The challenged findings concern what happened or what the evidence established.
predicates.findings_are_supported_by_evidence: The courts’ findings are supported by evidence presented in the case.
predicates.issue_was_understood_and_litigated: The parties understood the issue and presented their respective cases and evidence on it.

issues.definition: When a special-leave appeal challenges concurrent factual findings that are supported by evidence on an issue understood and litigated by the parties, those findings are left undisturbed.
